sentences.en: I lived in Athens, Georgia for a few years in the mid-90s.
sentences.zh: 我在 90 年代中期曾在佐治亚州的雅典市住过几年。

sentences.zh: 这座相当朴素的三柱式黑色金属拱门，

and it stands at the top of a couple of stone stairs
that marks the entrance to the campus.
Long, long ago it was connected to a fence,
sentences.zh: 很久很久以前，它曾连接着一道栅栏，

那就是智慧、正义和节制。

sentences.en: But it could matter for a different reason.

sentences.en: And that reason is adverse possession.
sentences.zh: 那个原因就是“逆权侵占”。

sentences.en: Adverse possession is an ancient legal principle that still exists today
sentences.zh: 逆权侵占是一项古老的法律原则，至今仍然存在，

sentences.en: under which a person who does not have legal title to a piece of land
sentences.zh: 根据该原则，一个对某块土地没有合法所有权的人，

sentences.en: may acquire legal ownership based on continuous possession
sentences.zh: 可以通过持续占有或使用该房产，

sentences.en: or occupation of the property without the permission of the legal owner.
sentences.zh: 在未经合法所有者许可的情况下获得合法所有权。

sentences.en: Basically, if the owner doesn't kick someone off the property,
sentences.zh: 简单来说，如果所有者不把人赶走，

sentences.en: then the squatter can legally become the new owner after a certain amount of time.
sentences.zh: 那么非法占用者在经过一定时间后，可以在法律上成为新的所有者。

sentences.en: There are lots of conditions and requirements,
but the existence of adverse possession is the reason you see little plaques on sidewalks
sentences.zh: 但逆权侵占的存在，就是为什么你会看到人行道上有小牌子，

sentences.en: that grant permission for people to pass over it,
even though it is private property,
and explicitly states that it will still remain private property of the original owner
sentences.zh: 并且明确声明，无论人们是否从上面通过，

sentences.en: no matter if people pass over it or not.
sentences.zh: 它仍将保持原所有者的私人财产地位。

sentences.en: So gates also function like this.

sentences.en: But really, only if you can close them and deny someone continuous possession.
sentences.zh: 但实际上，只有当你能关上门并拒绝他人持续占有时才有效。
